# 200. Number of Islands

[LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/) · **Medium** · Pattern: [Graphs](README.md) · [All patterns](../README.md) · [Home](../../README.md)

> **Key insight:** Each unvisited land cell starts a new island; flood-fill it to zeros so it is never counted again.

## Approach

1. Each unvisited land cell starts a new island; flood-fill it to zeros so it is never counted again.
2. Complexity: time `O(rows * cols)`, space `O(rows * cols)`.

| | Complexity |
|---|---|
| Time | `O(rows * cols)` |
| Space | `O(rows * cols)` |

## Solution

<!-- prep:solutions:start -->
<details>
<summary><b>Python</b> (spoiler) · <code>0200-number-of-islands.py</code></summary>

```python
from typing import List


class Solution:
    def numIslands(self, grid: List[List[str]]) -> int:
        rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])

        def sink(r: int, c: int) -> None:
            grid[r][c] = "0"
            stack = [(r, c)]
            while stack:
                r, c = stack.pop()
                for nr, nc in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                    if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and grid[nr][nc] == "1":
                        grid[nr][nc] = "0"  # mark on push, not on pop
                        stack.append((nr, nc))

        count = 0
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(cols):
                if grid[r][c] == "1":
                    count += 1
                    sink(r, c)
        return count
```

</details>
<!-- prep:solutions:end -->

## Mistakes and edge cases

- recursion depth error on a big grid; rewrote iteratively
- forgot to mark cells when pushing, duplicates
